newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi minister assails U.S. - papers.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi minister assails U.S. - papers.

text.p: Iraqi Culture and Information Minister Hamed Youssef Hummadi on Saturday harshly criticised U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, saying her recent statement on Iraq was "insolent".
Hummadi also said it was better for the U.S. administration to choose "the road of dialogue" with Iraq rather than the "road of confrontation."

"It is correct the language of (Albright's) statement is insolent...but it is also right that the language of insolence expresses failure, disability and frustration," Hummadi said in an editorial published by the official al-Qadissiya newspaper.
He said the United States and "Zionism" had recently esclated the situation against Iraq because they had failed to bring it under their influence.
Albright said on Wednesday the United States intended to back a political opposition in Iraq and made an explicit U.S. commitment to improve ties with a new government in Baghdad.

"This administration, through influence from the Zionist establishment, has chosen the road of confrontation (with Iraq) instead of the road of dialogue which is the civilised road of settling problems among nations," Hummadi added.
He also said the United States would block any lifting of U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said Albright was "intervening in Iraq's internal affairs in a savage manner just like that of the mafia men of America".
The paper accused the U.S. administration of creating problems for Iraq in order to colonise it.
